title: Hollow Sound
lede: A record label that presses 400 copies of everything needed a system that could hold 400 different records.
body: Hollow Sound came to me with eleven releases and eleven unrelated sleeves. The catalogue looked like a compilation of other labels. I built an identity around a single generative device: a set of concentric arcs whose spacing is driven by the length of the record, so every sleeve is different and every sleeve is obviously theirs.
The wordmark is drawn, not set - a tight grotesk with a hollowed counter in the O that reappears as the label's pressing mark on the centre labels and the spine of the box sets.
quote: Every sleeve is different. Every sleeve is obviously theirs.

title: Meridian Type Foundry
deliverables: Brand system, specimen book, e-commerce site
lede: A foundry storefront where the type does the selling, and nothing else is allowed to compete with it.
body: Meridian had a superb library and a shop that buried it under interface. I rebuilt the site around a single idea: the tester is the page. Every screen is typeset in the family you are looking at, at the size you choose, in the words you type.
The printed specimen followed - 96 pages, uncoated, one weight per spread, with the italic given the room it usually gets denied.

title: Northbound Coffee
deliverables: Identity, bag system, cafe signage, van livery
lede: Twelve origins, one shelf, and a three-second window to tell them apart.
body: The brief was retail-first: bags that read from two metres and still reward a close look. I coded each origin with a contour-line field derived from the elevation of the farm - the higher the grow, the tighter the lines.
Everything prints in two spot colours on unbleached kraft, which kept the range affordable to extend. Fourteen SKUs later it still holds.
quote: The higher the grow, the tighter the lines.

title: Atlas Athletic
deliverables: Campaign system, OOH, film titles, social
lede: A launch campaign built to survive being cropped, compressed and reposted.
body: I designed the campaign as a set of rules rather than a set of layouts: a fixed diagonal, a locked type scale, and one colour that never appears anywhere else in the category.
The result runs from a 48-sheet billboard down to a 1080×1080 crop without redrawing, which is what let the client ship six markets in eleven weeks.
quote: Rules, not layouts. That is what survives a crop.

title: Verso Press
lede: Twenty-two titles that had to look like a library, not a shelf of strangers.
body: A modernist series grid: one geometric plate per title, drawn from the book's subject, sitting in a fixed field with the author's name always in the same place.
Booksellers can stack them in any order and the spines still build a pattern. That was the whole argument for the format, and it sold the series in.
quote: Stack them in any order - the spines still build a pattern.

title: Field Notes Festival
lede: Three days, thirty acts, one halftone that gets denser as the weekend goes on.
body: The system is a single dot field whose density maps to the schedule - sparse on Friday afternoon, nearly solid by Saturday night. Print it big and it is an image; print it small and it is a texture.
Each act gets its own crop of the field, so thirty posters stay individual while reading as one festival from across the street.
quote: Print it big, it is an image. Print it small, it is a texture.

title: Kestrel Bank
deliverables: Design system, iOS & web app, brand refresh
lede: A banking app for people who do not enjoy banking apps.
body: I stripped the product back to three screens people actually use and rebuilt the design system around legibility: one typeface, four sizes, a contrast floor of 7:1 and no decorative colour anywhere near a number.
The system ships as tokens the client's engineers own, which is the only way a design system survives its first year.
quote: No decorative colour anywhere near a number.

title: Salt & Ash
lede: A wood-fire restaurant whose identity had to look good with a thumbprint on it.
body: Everything is letterpressed or foiled on stock that takes a mark well, because it will get marked. The ring device is struck slightly off-register on purpose - it looks better after a service than before one.
The menu is reprinted daily in-house from a two-colour template, so the kitchen can change a dish at 4pm without calling me.
quote: It looks better after a service than before one.

title: Jean Dawson Collection
services: Art direction, Apparel graphics, Poster design, Lettering
deliverables: Two tee graphics, four posters, collection graphics
lede: A self-initiated collection built around one artist’s visual world - garment graphics, posters and cut-up illustration running on a single printing language.
body: The starting question was what a run of merch would look like if it were designed the way a record sleeve is designed, rather than as a licensing exercise. Everything in the collection is built from the same kit: halftone and risograph texture, cut-up photography, and lettering drawn by hand instead of set.

Two garments anchor it. A washed green tee carries a drawn football helmet, its facemask broken into a spectrum; a washed black tee carries a photo collage under graffiti-weight lettering. Both graphics are built for the wash - heavy texture and open mid-tones, so the print reads worn rather than new on the first day.

The posters run on tight palettes: one green, one orange, one single-colour collage, and a four-colour sheet that pulls the whole series together. Held to a few inks each, they hang as a set on a wall while every sheet still stands on its own.
A self-initiated, conceptual project. Ace Studios is not affiliated with, or commissioned by, Jean Dawson - these designs are a personal exploration, made as a study of the artist’s work.
quote: Designed the way a record sleeve is designed, not as a licensing exercise.

title: Lacuna
services: Apparel graphics, Lettering, Art direction, Campaign
deliverables: Hoodie and tee graphics, wordmark, lookbook, storefront banner
lede: A streetwear line built on one hand-drawn wordmark, stretched across hoodies, tees and a lookbook.
body: The wordmark is drawn rather than set - a fast, marker-weight script that runs wide across a hoodie back, sits small at a tee hem, and wraps a globe on a back print without losing its hand.

The tee graphic pushes the other way: a swollen display letterform screened as an open halftone in a single green, with EMBRACE THE VOID set under it in a thin grotesk and deliberately knocked out of alignment.
Everything is drawn for garment-dyed blanks. Open halftones and mid-weight coverage settle into the wash rather than sitting on top of it, so the print reads worn from the first day.

The campaign banner runs the other way to the garment shots: the back print held small in a wide, warm frame with the space left open beside it, so the same artwork carries a storefront header without a crop fighting the type.
quote: Drawn rather than set, so it keeps its hand at any size.

title: 480 BC
deliverables: Tee and shorts graphics, brand mark
lede: An apparel capsule built around the Battle of Thermopylae, with line-drawn armour and a mark cut from the same hand.
body: The mark is a compressed, angular 480 that reads as much like a sigil as a number. It sits small on the chest, large on the leg, and holds at either size because the strokes are cut at a single angle.

The garment graphics are all line: a helmet drawn in one weight and broken so it wraps the side seam of the tee, and a pair of gorillas squared off across the front of the shorts. A second colourway drops the contrast to a tonal print on black.
A block of text about the battle is set small at the hem. It gives the capsule its name and does the explaining, so the graphics do not have to.
quote: The text at the hem does the explaining, so the graphics do not have to.
